title: Genuina principia doctrinae de statu aequilibrii et motu corporum tam perfecte flesibilium quam elasticorum

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Problema generale, Solutio §§I–III). A thread AMB, either perfectly flexible or elastic, is fixed at A and B, loaded by arbitrary forces, and in equilibrium. The aim is to find the state of tension or bending of every element.

§I. If the thread were cut at M, the pieces AM and BM would at once take different shapes. So, while they are joined, some force exists at M that resists separation and keeps the equilibrium shape.

§II (cut principle). Imagine AM actually cut off. Ask what forces must be applied at M so that BM keeps exactly the same configuration. That applied system is identified with the internal action that existed at M before the cut. Knowing it at every point gives the internal state of every element. In modern terms, the contact force (and, as the next page makes clear, the contact couple) at a cross-section is defined as the load system that replaces the removed part.

§III (pinning or rigidification argument). Suppose that force has been found and applied at M. The same force still keeps BM in its configuration if BM is additionally pinned (clavus, uncus) at any point C, or at several points, because pinning that does not alter the shape changes nothing. Push this to pinning at the neighbouring point m. The force needed at M is then still the one required as if BM were free and fixed only at B.

What it serves. §IV on the next page draws the consequence. With m pinned, only the element Mm is free, so the admissible forces at M are those that pull Mm away from m or bend it about m. This localises the problem to the constitutive behaviour of a single element:
- For a perfectly flexible thread, no bending action is admissible, so the force is tangential (tension along mMT).
- For an elastic thread (§V), there must also be an oblique force whose moment sustains the curvature. The curvature is measured by the contingence angle Tmt.

This is the derivation of the general balance equations for strings and rods. These have a contact force with tangential and transverse (shear) parts plus a bending moment proportional to curvature.
errors: The pinning argument (§III) gives a necessary condition, not a uniqueness proof. Once BM is pinned at extra points it is statically redundant, so the force at M is no longer determined by equilibrium alone. Euler uses only that the true internal force must still be an admissible equilibrating load when Mm alone is free. This is legitimate, but tacitly assumes that the internal action is local, i.e. a force-plus-couple determined by the element itself.

Minor: Euler speaks of 'vis' in the singular but 'vires' in §II. The internal action is in fact a force system (resultant force plus couple), as he concedes in §V. This is not an error, just loose wording at this point.

ideas.what: Internal action at a section defined as the load that must replace the cut-off part to preserve the configuration of the remainder
ideas.modern_name: Euler's cut principle / method of sections / contact-force principle for one-dimensional bodies
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (James Bernoulli and Hermann used it implicitly; Truesdell highlights Euler's explicit general formulation)
ideas.where_published: E410 itself (Novi Comm. Petrop. 15, 1771); discussed in Truesdell, The Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies 1638–1788 (Opera omnia II.11.2); later generalised in Euler's work on rigid and continuous bodies

ideas.what: Fixing additional points of an equilibrium configuration (without changing its shape) does not change the required internal action; pinning at the neighbouring point localises the problem to one element
ideas.modern_name: Solidification / rigidification principle (constraints compatible with the equilibrium configuration preserve equilibrium)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stevin (solidification); Euler, Lagrange in general form

ideas.what: Localisation to the element Mm leading to constitutive restrictions: tangential tension for flexible threads; force plus moment for elastic threads (completed on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Contact force and contact couple in rods; constitutive distinction between string and Euler–Bernoulli rod

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known foundational passage of E410 that Truesdell analysed in detail as Euler's general statement of the cut and contact-force principle for strings and rods. Nothing on the page appears to be absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'in statuo suo retinendum' is a misprint in the original (the scan has a correction-type mark between the words); read 'in statu suo retinendum'.
'etiamnunc' is printed 'etiamnúnc' in the original; this is immaterial.
The transcription is otherwise faithful to the image.
